arxiv-1907-10507.title: Modified Zero Forcing Decoder for Ill-conditioned Channels
arxiv-1907-10507.creator: Ibrahim Al-Nahhal, Masoud Alghoniemy, Adel B. Abd El-Rahman, Zen Kawasaki
arxiv-1907-10507.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Ibrahim Al-Nahhal, Masoud Alghoniemy, Adel B. Abd El-Rahman, Zen Kawasaki. A modified zero forcing decoder (MZF) for Multi-Input Multi-Output (MIMO) systems in case of ill-conditioned channels is proposed. The proposed decoder provides significant performance improvement compared to the traditional zero forcing for ill-conditioned channels. The proposed decoder is the result of reformulating the Q ​ R QR decomposition of the channel matrix by neglecting the elements which represent the correlation in the channel.

arxiv-2012-12767.title: Schrödinger cats in quantum-dot–cavity systems
arxiv-2012-12767.creator: M. Cosacchi, T. Seidelmann, J. Wiercinski, M. Cygorek, A. Vagov, D. E. Reiter, V. M. Axt
arxiv-2012-12767.description: Abstract A Schrödinger-cat state is a coherent superposition of macroscopically distinguishable quantum states, in quantum optics usually realized as superposition of coherent states. Protocols to prepare photonic cats have been presented for atomic systems. Here, we investigate in what manner and how well the preparation protocols can be transferred to a solid state platform, namely a semiconductor quantum-dot–cavity system.

arxiv-2106-13515.title: Ultralong temporal coherence in optically trapped exciton-polariton condensates
arxiv-2106-13515.creator: K. Orfanakis, A.F. Tzortzakakis, D. Petrosyan, P.G. Savvidis, H. Ohadi
arxiv-2106-13515.description: Abstract We investigate an optically trapped exciton-polariton condensate and observe temporal coherence beyond 1 ns duration. Due to the reduction of the spatial overlap with the thermal reservoir of excitons, the coherence time of the trapped condensate is more than an order of magnitude longer than that of an untrapped condensate.

arxiv-2108-07299.title: Dirac type relativistic quantum mechanics for massive photons
arxiv-2108-07299.creator: Soon-Tae Hong
arxiv-2108-07299.description: Abstract Constructing a relativistic quantum mechanics (RQM) for a massive photon, without appealing to the quantum field theoretical approach such as the massive Proca model, we find a new theoretical particle solution which allows the massive photon having either positive or negative energy as solutions.

arxiv-2205-01097.title: Generalization of the basis theorem for the D D -type Coxeter groups
arxiv-2205-01097.creator: Sawsan Khaskeia, Robert Shwartz
arxiv-2205-01097.description: Abstract The O ​ G ​ S OGS for non-abelian groups is an interesting generalization of the basis of finite abelian groups. The definition of O ​ G ​ S OGS states that every element of a group has a unique presentation as a product of some powers of specific generators of the group, in a specific given order.

arxiv-2207-03053.title: Pattern Formation and Front Stability for a Moving-Boundary Model of Biological Invasion and Recession Journal: Physica D: Nonlinear Phenomena.
arxiv-2207-03053.creator: Alexander K. Y. Tam, Matthew J. Simpson
arxiv-2207-03053.description: Abstract We investigate pattern formation in a two-dimensional (2D) Fisher–Stefan model, which involves solving the Fisher–KPP equation on a compactly-supported region with a moving boundary. The boundary evolves analogously to the classical Stefan problem, such that boundary speed is proportional to the local population density gradient.

arxiv-2510-15686.title: Few-Shot Demonstration-Driven Task Coordination and Trajectory Execution for Multi-Robot Systems
arxiv-2510-15686.creator: Taehyeon Kim † {\dagger}, Vishnunandan L.N. Venkatesh † {\dagger}, Byung-Cheol Min
arxiv-2510-15686.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a novel few-shot learning framework for multi-robot systems that integrate both spatial and temporal elements: Few-Shot Demonstration-Driven Task Coordination and Trajectory Execution (DDACE). Our approach leverages temporal graph networks for learning task-agnostic temporal sequencing and Gaussian Processes for spatial trajectory modeling, ensuring modularity and generalization across various tasks.

pmc-12558277.title: Assessing the relationship between gut microbiota and hyperprolactinemia: A bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization study
pmc-12558277.creator: Teng Qi, Yujie Hu, Xiaorui Zhou, Lanhui Zhang, Xulong Zhu, Mingkun Zhang, Zhenping Ouyang, Miao Wei, Sujin Wang, Chuanlin Zhao, Fuqing Ji
pmc-12558277.description: The relationship between hyperprolactinemia and gut microbiota remains unclear at present. This study employs a Mendelian randomization (MR) approach to assess the potential causal links between gut microbiota and the incidence of hyperprolactinemia. Genetic instrumental variables associated with gut microbiota were identified through a genome-wide association study involving 18,340 participants.

pmc-13204162.title: Adenosine Signaling as a Central Integrative Network in Cellular Stress Responses and a Therapeutically Actionable Target in Human Disease
pmc-13204162.creator: Shakta Mani Satyam, Mohamed El-Tanani, Wasim Iyad Alghoul, Malak Moones Abedi, Shabil Fathah Farook, Ibrahim Khalil Alabid, Mohammed Dalbah, Natasha Nasser, Samreen Fazal, Mariam Radhi Al-Talqani, Mohammed Mahmood Ali, Ebrahim Safaii, Wed Burhan Jameel Al-Shammari, Burhanuddin Murtaza Patanwala
pmc-13204162.description: Adenosine has emerged as a central metabolic signal linking cellular stress to systemic physiological adaptation. Under conditions such as hypoxia, ischemia, inflammation, and tissue injury, extracellular adenosine triphosphate (eATP) released from stressed cells is sequentially metabolized by the ectonucleotidases CD39 and CD73, generating adenosine that accumulates in the extracellular microenvironment.

pmc-13254505.title: Developing Customized Personas to Capture Intrinsic Capacity Profiles and Digital Monitoring Intentions in Older Adults: Mixed Methods Study
pmc-13254505.creator: Zehui Xuan, Yirou Niu, Ruifu Kang, Qian Xiao, Shuai Jin, Jie Zhao, Yanling Wang, Hong Chang, Jinjiao Wang, Giulio Amabili, Xiaoli Yuan
pmc-13254505.description: BackgroundIntegrated Care for Older People (ICOPE), focused on monitoring and optimizing the intrinsic capacity (IC) of older adults, is a new model of geriatric care that is currently being accelerated globally. Digital health technologies are recommended for longitudinal IC monitoring to provide precise and timely interventions.

pmc-13507548.title: Strontium-incorporated thermoresponsive hydrogel platform co-delivering graphene oxide-mannose nanocomplexes: An osteoimmunomodulatory strategy for periodontitis therapy
pmc-13507548.creator: Linxin Chen, Jiayi Cai, Lin Liu, Geyuan Zheng, Sihang Chen, Maotuan Huang, Linyu Xu, Wenxiu Yuan
pmc-13507548.description: Periodontitis is an immune-mediated disease that destroys tooth-supporting tissues, yet existing treatments cannot synchronize inflammation resolution with bone regeneration. To address this unmet need, we report an injectable, strontium-incorporated an injectable thermoresponsive hydrogel (composed of chitosan, 0.6% gelatin, and β-glycerophosphate) platform engineered for the delivery of graphene oxide-mannose nanocomplexes (designated GM-Sr@Hydrogel).

pmc-13584130.title: Burosumab improves alkaline phosphatase and rickets severity in X-linked hypophosphatemia: 3-year SUNFLOWER analysis
pmc-13584130.creator: Keiichi Ozono, Hee Gyung Kang, Noriyuki Namba, Nobuaki Ito, Takuo Kubota, Ayumi Shintani, Ryota Kawai, Osamu Miyazaki, Masanori Kanematsu, Haruka Ishii, Toshimi Michigami
pmc-13584130.description: SUNFLOWER is a 10-year longitudinal observational cohort study of patients with X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH) in Japan and South Korea. This report describes the 3-year cut-off of SUNFLOWER, including data from 1 year of burosumab administration (burosumab-treated group) and 1 year after providing informed consent (non-burosumab-treated group).

uslaw-usc-t39-s3662.title: 39 U.S.C. § 3662 — Rate and service complaints
uslaw-usc-t39-s3662.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t39-s3662.description: United States Code, Title 39 (Postal Service); Part IV (Mail Matter); Chapter 36 (Postal Rates, Classes, And Services); Subchapter V (Postal Services, Complaints, And Judicial Review). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) In General.— Any interested person (including an officer of the Postal Regulatory Commission representing the interests of the general public) who believes the Postal Service is not operating in conformance.

uslaw-usc-t40-s17902.title: 40 U.S.C. § 17902 — Sale of electric energy
uslaw-usc-t40-s17902.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t40-s17902.description: United States Code, Title 40 (Public Buildings, Property, And Works); Chapter 179 (Alaska Federal-Civilian Energy Efficiency Swap). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) In General.— To conserve oil and natural gas and better utilize coal, the head of a federal agency may sell, or enter into a contract to sell, to any non-federal person electric energy generated by coal-fired electric generating facilities.
